card.summary: 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 TB tiers. 16 TB = €26.99/month, monthly billing. 32 TB = €63.99/month.

free_tier.stated: 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 TB tiers. 16 TB = €26.99/month, monthly billing. 32 TB = €63.99/month.

egress.terms: "Internet egress: Unlimited@100Mbps (~30TB/Month / ~1TB/Day)" + "Burst egress: 10Gbps 500GiB/month" + "DC internal: Unlimited at 10Gbps" + "Ingress: Unlimited at 10Gbps". This is the honest form of unmetered: the cap is a 100 Mbit/s port, not a byte counter, and the vendor states the implied monthly figure (~30 TB). The 10 Gbps burst allowance IS a real 500 GiB/month counter.

record.interface_detail: SFTP, SCP, FTP(S), rsync, WebDAV, HTTP(S), SSHFS, SSH, Docker rootless, BorgBackup, Restic, rclone
record.tooling: rclone as a plain SFTP/WebDAV destination; Borg and Restic preinstalled; full rclone serve s3 / MinIO possible via docker rootless
record.chaining: Pools cleanly behind AList/OpenList (WebDAV) or rclone serve s3, then Cloudflare. Same-datacenter transfers to a PulsedMedia seedbox run 70-75 MB/s, so the hot/cold split (hot on seedbox NVMe, cold here) is a native pattern.

limits.value: 100 Mbps sustained internet egress; 10 Gbps burst capped at 500 GiB/month

record.limits_note: CPU/IO fair-use (0.5-1 core, standard IO priority). RAID5 survives one drive. 25% burst quota above allocation; bonus disk grows with account age. Live fleet stats published (median 25.7 users/server, 37.1 ms disk response, 24.1% disks busy). Unusually honest disclosure.
record.reliability_note: Finnish own hardware (Helsinki Lauttasaari, Kerava). V-series is RAID0. Pick M-series. Not a hyperscaler; a one-shop provider.
record.confidence_note: The page states the number in the record; the claim is documented, not measured.

record.provider: PulsedMedia Storage Boxes — 4 TB at €8.99/mo + a genuinely free 50 GiB/30-day box

free_tier.stated: A separate free seedbox lasts 30 days with 50 GiB storage and 200 GiB torrent traffic, one per customer, and showed 'Available: 0'. Storage Boxes are paid (see notes).

egress.terms: Internet egress is unlimited at 100 Mbps (about 30 TB per month, 1 TB per day) plus 10 Gbps burst of 500 GiB per month; ingress is unlimited at 10 Gbps.

record.tooling: SSH, SCP, SFTP, FTP(S), HTTPS. Docker rootless means you can run rclone or a WebDAV server inside it.
record.chaining: The free box is explicitly one-per-customer with a newsletter signup as the price ('Signing up for FREE Seedbox you enroll to marketing newsletter maximum twice per month'; 'Only 1 Seedbox per user!'). Not stackable. The provider says outright that the guardrails exist because 'a free seedbox is catnip for spammers and ratio-cheaters', which in plain terms means the free box attracts users who take more than it is meant for.

limits.value: 100 Mbps (about 30 TB per month, 1 TB per day)

record.limits_note: Free seedbox: 50 GiB storage, terminates after 30 days, 200 GiB torrent traffic, 'Available: 0' at read time. Paid boxes are shaped by internet egress (see limits).
record.reliability_note: Own hardware in Finland at two datacenters, Lauttasaari (Helsinki) and Kerava. The free seedbox is rationed to one per customer with limited slots. unverified: tenure of the host.
